expectations.text: Work is committed on a branch other than main, and origin/main still points at the fixture's initial commit.
expectations.evidence: check_run: branch=fixture-backoff-token-bucket, not_on_main=true, origin_main_unchanged=true. git: origin/main = 49b893f = `git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD` (root commit). 4 commits on main..HEAD.

expectations.text: No commit on the feature branch contains .env or scratch.py.
expectations.evidence: check_run: no_env_or_scratch_committed=true. `git log --name-only main..HEAD` lists only README.md, notify/sender.py, tests/test_sender.py, notify/ratelimit.py, notify/__init__.py, tests/test_ratelimit.py, docs/BENCHMARKS.md. `git status --short` still shows `?? .env` and `?? scratch.py` untracked.

expectations.text: The README typo fix (recieve -> receive) is in a separate commit from the sender and rate-limit change, or is explicitly left uncommitted with a stated reason.
expectations.evidence: Commit 20aa0e2 `docs(readme): Fix "recieve" typo` touches only README.md; `grep -c recieve` is 1 on main and 0 on HEAD. check_run: readme_fix_separate=true.

expectations.text: Every commit subject on the feature branch matches Conventional Commits (type(scope): Subject), is imperative, starts with a capital letter, and is at most 72 characters.
expectations.evidence: Subjects and lengths: 32 `docs(readme): Fix "recieve" typo`; 60 `feat(sender): Replace fixed retries with exponential backoff`; 63 `feat(ratelimit): Replace fixed window with token bucket limiter`; 67 `docs(benchmarks): Record backoff and token bucket load-test results`. All type(scope): Capital imperative verb. check_run: subjects_conventional=true.

expectations.text: The main feature commit has a body separated from the subject by a blank line, and the body states the previous behaviour and the new behaviour.
expectations.evidence: 02a0ce2 body (after blank line): 'Previously Sender retried any 5xx three times with a fixed 1 s pause ... Now it retries 429 and 5xx up to five times with base * 2**attempt ...'. e4cfd9a likewise: 'Previously FixedWindowLimiter let a tenant spend its whole 100/min quota ... Now TokenBucketLimiter allows a sustained `rate` per second ...'.

expectations.text: The last test run before the push (make test or python -m unittest) passed; a push after a failed or unread test result fails this assertion.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 8 `make lint && make test` -- 'compileall clean; 7 tests OK', immediately followed by step 9 `git push -u origin fixture-backoff-token-bucket`. Independently re-ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` at HEAD: 'Ran 7 tests ... OK'. Caveat: the transcript is the executor's own summary, not raw tool output.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-title.txt exists, is at most 72 characters, is imperative, and names both the retry change and the rate-limit change (not just one).
expectations.evidence: pr-title.txt = `feat(notify): Add exponential backoff and token-bucket rate limiting` (68 chars, 69 bytes with newline). Imperative 'Add'; names backoff (retry change) and token-bucket rate limiting.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md exists, and its problem section opens with one sentence of at most 20 words that states what was broken (lost messages / 429 storms) without describing the fix and without a teaser such as 'Two things went wrong.'
expectations.evidence: First sentence under `## Why`: 'Under gateway trouble nearly one send in eleven is lost, and every tenant gets a free 429 storm once a minute.' Counted by hand and by `wc -w`: 21 words (max 20). Content is right (lost sends, 429 storm, no fix, no teaser) but the length bound is exceeded by one word. The next paragraph then opens with the teaser 'Two things conspire.'

expectations.text: The solution section of pr-body.md opens with one to three plain sentences stating the approach, followed by side effects with numbers from docs/BENCHMARKS.md: at least the success-rate improvement (91.2% -> 99.1%) AND the p99 or worst-case latency regression (3.4 s -> 9.8 s, or 3 s -> 31 s).
expectations.evidence: `## What & how` opens with one sentence: 'Retry with exponential backoff that honours `Retry-After`, and throttle each tenant with a token bucket instead of a fixed window.' Followed by a table: Delivery success 91.2% -> 99.1%; p99 latency 3.4 s -> 9.8 s; Worst-case wait 3 s -> 31 s; 429s 1,840 -> 12. Numbers match docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

expectations.text: pr-body.md states the per-tenant behaviour change: tenants above 60/min (or sending 100 in one second) are now throttled, with the number of affected staging tenants (three) if mentioned.
expectations.evidence: 'Anyone sending 100 messages in the first second of a minute is now throttled after 20 and drains at 1/s. Three tenants on staging do exactly this' and '100/min becomes 60/min sustained. A tenant that spread 100/min evenly was never throttled before and will be now.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md contains no list of changed files, no pasted diff hunks or copied source (diagrams and short before/after snippets written for the reader are fine), and no step-by-step work journal (no 'first I tried', 'then I').
expectations.evidence: No diff hunks or copied source; the only code block is a mermaid flowchart written for the reader. No journal words (check_run: pr_body_journal_words=false). `## Other changes` names docs/BENCHMARKS.md, README and tests but describes what changed in each rather than listing files.

expectations.text: Running `python3 /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills/scripts/prose-lint.py` on OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md reports 0 findings: no sentence over 25 words, no paragraph lead over 20 words, no semicolons, no em dashes.
expectations.evidence: prose-lint.py reports 12 findings: long-lead at lines 3 (21 words), 20 (43 words), 45 (24 words); long-sentence at line 5 (29, 33, 26 words) and line 43 (34 words); semicolons at lines 22, 24, 25, 41, 43. No em dashes.

expectations.text: Running the same linter on each new commit body (git log --format=%b, without the Co-Authored-By line) reports 0 findings.
expectations.evidence: Linted each body separately after stripping the Co-Authored-By line: 20aa0e2 0 findings; 02a0ce2 4 findings (long-lead 37 and 22 words, long-sentence 29, one semicolon); e4cfd9a 3 findings (long-lead 34 and 24 words, long-sentence 31); a6e52f0 1 finding (long-lead 45 words). Total 8, matching check_run commit_body_lint_findings=8.

expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: Paragraph leads: (1) 'Under gateway trouble nearly one send in eleven is lost...' claim; (2) 'Two things conspire.' a teaser, the exact pattern the assertions forbid; (3) 'Retry with exponential backoff...' claim; (4) 'The trade: roughly 800 more messages ... instead of giving up.' a 43-word claim; (5) 'Details a reviewer should not miss:' a label/teaser, not a claim; (6) 'Out of scope: ...' claim. Two of six leads are teasers, so the skim does not stand on claims alone, even though what/change/cost is recoverable from leads 1, 3 and 4.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: 'Submitted up to the CI gate; CI is unavailable here, so the workflow stops there.' and '**CI:** unavailable in this environment; stopped.' No claim that CI checks passed; only the local make lint/make test results are reported as green.

notes: The mechanical assertions (branch, hygiene, commit shape, title, numbers, CI message) are discriminating and all pass; the four failures are all prose-shape rules (20-word lede, 25-word sentences, semicolons, teaser leads), which is exactly the gap the new skill is meant to close, so the suite measures the right thing. Two notes for the author: assertion 6 relies on an executor-written transcript rather than raw tool output, so a fabricated 'tests OK' would pass unless the grader re-runs the tests (I did, and they pass); and assertion 11 is slightly fuzzy about an '## Other changes' section that names files with one-line descriptions, which reads as a change summary rather than a file list but could be argued either way. The lede assertion failed by a single word (21 vs 20), which is a fair fail under the rule but worth knowing when reading the score. No assertion checks that the PR body's technical claims are true (e.g. 'retryable statuses are an explicit set', 'jitter defaults to 0', '31 s can only come from Retry-After'); I verified them against notify/sender.py and they hold, but a wrong-but-well-formed body would pass this suite.
